insider_note: eˣ sinx dx is the one standard integral in this chapter where by-parts must be applied TWICE and the original integral reappears on the right — solving for it algebraically, exactly like a reduction formula, is the method that finishes it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Apply integration by parts twice
lines: So I = sinx·eˣ − [cosx·eˣ + I] = eˣ(sinx−cosx) − I
steps.why: Applying by-parts a SECOND time to the leftover ∫cosx eˣdx brings the ORIGINAL integral I back, since differentiating twice returns eˣ sinx again — this is what makes the algebra close.
common_mistakes: Stopping after the first by-parts step, leaving ∫cosx eˣ dx un-integrated.
Losing track of the sign when the second by-parts application produces +∫sinx eˣ dx = +I.
steps.memory_tip: Two rounds of by-parts on eˣ times a trig function ALWAYS bring the original integral back — this is expected, not a mistake.

steps.label: Solve for the integral for the final answer
steps.why: With I appearing on both sides, collecting the two I terms on the left gives 2I, and dividing by 2 gives the final closed form.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to add the +I from the right side to the I on the left, and instead treating the equation as already solved.
Dropping the +c, which only appears once the equation is fully solved for I.
steps.memory_tip: I = … − I rearranges to 2I = … — exactly the same move used to solve a reduction formula for I_n.
